title: Open Problem (Introduction)
statement_text: Determine the correct dependence of $ES_{\ell}(n)$ on $\ell$.
context_text: A planar point set is in convex position if it is the vertex set of a convex polygon. For $\ell,n\ge3$, $ES_\ell(n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every set of $N$ points in the plane contains either $\ell$ collinear points or $n$ points in convex position; thus $ES_3(n)=ES(n)$ is the classical Erdős–Szekeres number for point sets in general position, for which $2^{n-2}+1\le ES(n)\le 4^{n+o(n)}$ (Erdős and Szekeres conjectured the lower bound to be tight, and Suk proved $ES(n)=2^{n+o(n)}$). The authors prove that there is a constant $C>0$ such that $(3\ell-1)\cdot2^{n-5}<ES_\ell(n)<\ell^2\cdot2^{n+C\sqrt{n\log n}}$ for all $\ell,n\ge3$, so the dependence on $\ell$ is between linear and quadratic. Their proof goes through a new cups-caps theorem for arbitrary point sets, which implies that for fixed $n$ and $\ell\to\infty$, $ES_\ell(n)=O(\ell)$, best possible up to constants; the joint dependence on $\ell$ remains open.
notes: Stated in running prose at the end of the introduction: "It remains an interesting open problem to determine the correct dependence of $ES_{\ell}(n)$ on $\ell$."
paper_title: Big line or big convex polygon
